section.heading: SHORT TITLE.
section.content: This Act may be cited as the “Lower Delaware Wild and Scenic Rivers Act”.

paragraph.content: Public Law 102–460 directed the Secretary of the Interior, in cooperation and consultation with appropriate Federal, State, regional, and local agencies, to conduct a study of the eligibility and suitability of the lower Delaware River for inclusion in the Wild and Scenic Rivers System;

during the study, the Lower Delaware Wild and Scenic River Study Task Force and the National Park Service prepared a river management plan for the study area entitled “Lower Delaware River Management Plan” and dated August 1997, which establishes goals and actions that will ensure long-term protection of the river's outstanding values and compatible management of land and water resources associated with the river; and

after completion of the study, 24 municipalities along segments of the Delaware River eligible for designation passed resolutions supporting the Lower Delaware River Management Plan, agreeing to take action to implement the goals of the plan, and endorsing designation of the river.

section.heading: DESIGNATION.
section.editorialNote: [Added a new paragraph at the end of section 3(a) of the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act (16 U.S.C. 1274(a)).]

subsection.heading: Management of Segments.—
subsection.chapeau: The river segments designated in section 3 shall be managed—

paragraph.content: in accordance with the river management plan entitled “Lower Delaware River Management Plan” and dated August 1997 (referred to as the “management plan”), prepared by the Lower Delaware Wild and Scenic River Study Task Force and the National Park Service, which establishes goals and actions that will ensure long-term protection of the river's outstanding values and compatible management of land and water resources associated with the river; and

paragraph.chapeau: in cooperation with appropriate Federal, State, regional, and local agencies, including—

subparagraph.content: the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection;
the Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources;
the Delaware and Lehigh Navigation Canal Heritage Corridor Commission;
the Delaware and Raritan Canal Commission; and

subsection.heading: Satisfaction of Requirements for Plan.—
subsection.content: The management plan shall be considered to satisfy the requirements for a comprehensive management plan under subsection 3(d) of the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act (16 U.S.C. 1274(d)).

paragraph.heading: Restrictions on water resource projects.—
paragraph.content: In determining under section 7(a) of the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act (16 U.S.C. 1278(a)) whether a proposed water resources project would have a direct and adverse effect on the value for which a segment is designated as part of the Wild and Scenic Rivers System, the Secretary of the Interior (hereinafter referred to as the “Secretary”) shall consider the extent to which the project is consistent with the management plan.

paragraph.heading: Cooperative agreements.—
paragraph.chapeau: Any cooperative agreements entered into under section 10(e) of the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act (16 U.S.C. 1281(e)) relating to any of the segments designated by this Act shall—

subparagraph.content: be consistent with the management plan; and
may include provisions for financial or other assistance from the United States to facilitate the long-term protection, conservation, and enhancement of the segments.

paragraph.heading: Support for implementation.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may provide technical assistance, staff support, and funding to assist in the implementation of the management plan.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may provide planning, financial, and technical assistance to local municipalities to assist in the implementation of actions to protect the natural, economic, and historic resources of the river segments designated by this Act.

paragraph.heading: Plan requirements.—
paragraph.content: After adoption of recommendations made in section III of the management plan, the zoning ordinances of the municipalities bordering the segments shall be considered to satisfy the standards and requirements under section 6(c) of the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act (16 U.S.C. 1277(c)).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: In this paragraph, the term “additional segment” means—

subparagraph.content: the segment from the Delaware Water Gap to the Toll Bridge connecting Columbia, New Jersey, and Portland, Pennsylvania (approximately 9.2 miles), which, if made part of the Wild and Scenic Rivers System in accordance with this paragraph, shall be administered by the Secretary as a recreational river;

the segment from the Erie Lackawanna railroad bridge to the southern tip of Dildine Island (approximately 3.6 miles), which, if made part of the Wild and Scenic Rivers System in accordance with this paragraph, shall be administered by the Secretary as a recreational river;

the segment from the southern tip of Mack Island to the northern border of the town of Belvidere, New Jersey (approximately 2 miles), which, if made part of the Wild and Scenic Rivers System in accordance with this paragraph, shall be administered by the Secretary as a recreational river;

the segment from the southern border of the town of Phillipsburg, New Jersey, to a point just north of Gilbert Generating Station (approximately 9.5 miles), which, if made part of the Wild and Scenic Rivers System in accordance with this paragraph, shall be administered by the Secretary as a recreational river;

Paulinskill River in Knowlton Township (approximately 2.4 miles), which, if made part of the Wild and Scenic Rivers System in accordance with this paragraph, shall be administered by the Secretary as a recreational river; and
Cook's Creek (approximately 3.5 miles), which, if made part of the Wild and Scenic Rivers System in accordance with this paragraph, shall be administered by the Secretary as a scenic river.

paragraph.heading: Finding.—
paragraph.content: Congress finds that each of the additional segments is suitable for designation as a recreational river or scenic river under this paragraph, if there is adequate local support for the designation.

paragraph.heading: Designation.—
paragraph.chapeau: If the Secretary finds that there is adequate local support for designating any of the additional segments as a recreational river or scenic river—

subparagraph.content: the Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register a notice of the designation of the segment; and
the segment shall thereby be designated as a recreational river or scenic river, as the case may be, in accordance with the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act (16 U.S.C. 1271 et seq.).

paragraph.heading: Criteria for local support.—
paragraph.content: In determining whether there is adequate local support for the designation of an additional segment, the Secretary shall consider, among other things, the preferences of local governments expressed in resolutions concerning designation of the segment.

section.heading: AUTHORIZATION OF APPROPRIATIONS.
section.content: There is authorized to be appropriated such sums as are necessary to carry out this Act.
